name: no-time
title: No Time to Type
kicker: Why I needed it twice over
html:
No Time to Type

Have you ever tried to write code with a leash in one hand? I don’t recommend it.

Half the Answer: /remote-control

The session runs on my machine. I steer it mostly by dictating into my phone.

The Other Half: Rigor Without Watching

BDD for real, the same way every time: Gherkin, red, code, green, commit.

Asking Nicely? Probably Not.

Instructions are advisory, so hooks enforce the order. I read the record afterward.

Notice that an agent calling an API needs the same thing: controls that still hold when nobody is watching. hooks.json

/remote-control

Please give me an update

Red run logged. Writing the fix.

How’s it going?

Green. Commit gate: TDD order checked.

🐕 pulling. back in 20

Illustrative, not a transcript. The two questions are the real ones, every evening. So is the dog.
say: Here's the 'twice over'. Have you ever tried to write code with a leash in one hand? I don't recommend it. Between family and a new dog, the time I used to spend at a keyboard is gone. Most of my work now is speech-to-text, dictated into my phone, through Claude Code's /remote-control, while the session runs on my machine. So I needed two things I could trust without watching. An agent that does the right thing, the same way, every time. And a way of building it where Claude does the right thing, in the right order, every time, while I'm not looking. Let's take the agent first: what did I want it to be?
